title: The useState Hook
description: Learn how to add state to functional components using the useState hook.

data.text: **State** is data that changes over time in your application. The `useState` hook is the most fundamental hook in React - it lets you add state to functional components.
`useState` returns an array with two values: the current state value and a function to update it. You destructure these values when calling the hook.

data.title: useState Basics

data.text: You can use `useState` multiple times in a single component to manage different pieces of state.

data.title: Multiple States

data.text: When storing objects in state, you need to create a new object when updating to ensure React detects the change.

data.title: Object State

data.text: When the new state depends on the previous state, use a function to ensure you always have the latest value.

data.title: Functional Updates
data.content: Using function form for state updates

data.title: Never Mutate State Directly
data.text: Always create new objects/arrays when updating state. React uses reference equality to detect changes, so mutating state directly won't trigger a re-render.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Never mutate state directly - always create new values
Use functional updates when new state depends on old state
You can have multiple useState calls in one component
data.takeaway: State powers dynamic UIs. Let's learn how to handle user events to update state.
